chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who sends a sacrificial animal voluntarily, not as an obligation. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He appoints a day with his companions, and they yoke it. When that time comes, he refrains from what the one in Ihram refrains from, until the Day of Sacrifice. When the Day of Sacrifice arrives, it suffices for him.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The one in Ihram (state of consecration)
key_terms.يُقَلِّدُونَهُ: They yoke it / put the yoke on it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for voluntarily sending a sacrificial animal and the required Ihram-like observances?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ritual status of a layperson sending a voluntary offering (hady) by mandating that he observe the prohibitions of Ihram from the appointed time until the Day of Sacrifice, ensuring the validity of the sacrifice. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of ritual purity and restriction for the sender, mirroring the state of the pilgrim, even when the animal is not physically present with him. This practice underscores the spiritual discipline required in voluntary acts of worship within the framework of Hajj and Umrah.
